I've been farming this land in Quzhou my whole life, and my father before me. The soil here on the North China Plain is good for one thing I know well: wheat in winter, maize in summer. That's the rotation. That's what I plant. I have about 8 mu of contracted land — nothing big, but it's mine to work.

For wheat, I'll sow in early October like always. I use Jimai 22 seed — I've grown it several years now, the yields are steady and it handles the cold well. I'll apply basal fertilizer before ploughing, then top-dress nitrogen at jointing. I water four times: the pre-winter irrigation, jointing, heading, and grain fill. Can't skip any of them here, the rains aren't reliable. I'll spray herbicide in spring and treat for aphids and powdery mildew before heading.

After wheat harvest in June, I'll plant summer maize right away — no-till, direct seeding into the stubble. Hybrid seed, Xianyu 335 or similar, whatever the local agro-supply shop has. Maize doesn't need as much fussing. Two irrigations if the summer is dry. I'll apply fertilizer at planting and side-dress at the big bell stage. One pass for pests, one for fall armyworm if it shows up again like last year.

At 62, I can still do this work, but I'll hire a neighbor's son to help at wheat harvest. The maize I'll machine-harvest in late September.
